passages.title: The Chalk Mark
passages.text: A dead drop is a way to pass a package without two people ever meeting. One person hides the item and leaves a signal nearby. The signal is usually small and dull, because a signal that draws attention defeats the whole method. A chalk mark on a lamp post is a common choice. The second person checks for the mark, collects the package later, and erases the mark on the way out. Handlers prefer this method in crowded places. A busy square gives a courier dozens of ordinary reasons to stop walking.

levels.name: Tradecraft
levels.goal: Read what the briefing actually says

items.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the passage?
choices: A dead drop lets two people exchange something without meeting.
Chalk marks are the most common signal used by couriers.
Crowded squares are dangerous places to pass a package.
Handlers erase their signals so nobody can follow them.
items.explain: The central idea is the point the whole passage is built to make, not the most interesting detail in it. Every paragraph here returns to one thing: a dead drop moves a package without a meeting. The chalk mark, the crowded square and the erasing are all evidence for that point rather than the point itself.

distractorRationale.1: picks a true detail and mistakes it for the main point; the chalk mark is one example of a signal, not what the passage is about
distractorRationale.2: reverses the passage, which says a busy square helps the courier rather than endangering them
distractorRationale.3: narrows to the last step in the process and misses the reason the process exists

partA.stem: Why do handlers want a signal that looks dull?
choices: So it is cheap to leave behind
So it does not attract attention
So it can be erased quickly
So other couriers can copy it

partB.stem: Which sentence from the passage best supports your answer?
choices: The signal is usually small and dull, because a signal that draws attention defeats the whole method.
A chalk mark on a lamp post is a common choice.
Handlers prefer this method in crowded places.
A busy square gives a courier dozens of ordinary reasons to stop walking.

items.explain: Part A asks for the reason, and the passage gives it directly: a signal that draws attention defeats the method. Part B is not asking which sentence is most interesting, it is asking which sentence would convince someone your Part A answer is right. Matching your evidence to your own answer is the habit being trained here, so keep the two consistent even when you are unsure.

distractorRationale.0: cost is never mentioned in the passage; this is real-world reasoning substituted for the text
distractorRationale.2: erasing appears in the passage but as a later step, not as the reason the signal is dull
distractorRationale.3: confuses copying with concealment; nothing in the passage is about other couriers reading the mark
